events.title: Council of Troyes Approves the Knights Templar
events.description: At the Council of Troyes in France, the Knights Templar were formally recognized as a religious military order, with Bernard of Clairvaux influential in drafting their Latin Rule.
events.significance: The Templars became one of the most powerful and wealthy Christian military orders of the Middle Ages, shaping Crusader-era warfare, banking, and politics.

events.title: Founding of the Independent Labour Party
events.description: The Independent Labour Party was founded at a conference in Bradford, England, with Keir Hardie as a leading figure, to give working people independent political representation.
events.significance: The ILP was a key precursor to the British Labour Party, which emerged in 1900, and shaped the growth of socialist and labour politics in Britain.

events.title: Zola Publishes 'J'Accuse...!'
events.description: Émile Zola's open letter to French President Félix Faure, titled 'J'Accuse...!', was published on the front page of the newspaper L'Aurore, accusing the army of covering up the wrongful conviction of Captain Alfred Dreyfus.
events.significance: The letter galvanized public opinion in the Dreyfus Affair, exposed institutional antisemitism and injustice, and became a landmark in the history of press freedom and public intellectual engagement.

events.title: First Public Radio Broadcast
events.description: Lee de Forest conducted an experimental public radio broadcast from the Metropolitan Opera House in New York City, transmitting live performances by Enrico Caruso and others.
events.significance: This early experiment demonstrated the potential of radio for mass entertainment and communication, foreshadowing the broadcasting industry.
